rationale.a: Window units are ideal for medium office buildings (500–1,000 m²) because they require no outdoor condenser installation.
rationale.b: Mini-splits are recommended for large residential complexes (>500 m²) as the primary cooling system due to lowest upfront cost.
rationale.d: Window/mini-split units should replace split-type systems in all residential applications because they occupy less indoor space.
rationale.correct: Window and mini-split units (0.5–2 TR) are best for small rooms, temporary spaces, and supplementary cooling in hard-to-reach zones where a full split or VRF system cannot be economically justified. Example: a 15 m² server closet, a single guest room in a hotel, or a temporary office annex. They should NOT be specified as primary cooling for buildings >100 m² or continuous-occupancy spaces. Source: ALE-UTIL-002-04 Module Window-Type and Mini-Split Units section.
rationale.takeaway: Window and mini-split units are supplementary, not primary, cooling solutions; best reserved for spot cooling, small rooms, or temporary facilities.
